payload.title: Italian Marriage Recognition in Australia Explained
payload.excerpt: Is marriage in Italy recognised in Australia? In most cases, yes: an overseas marriage is generally recognised here if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law, according to both Smartraveller and the Attorney-General's Department.
key_takeaways: An Italian marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid under Italian law and would have been valid here, the test set by Part VA of the Marriage Act 1961.
You cannot register an Italian marriage in Australia, so bring home the comune's (town hall's) marriage certificate with a Prefettura apostille and have it translated in full.
If you were born in Australia and want your partner's surname on your passport, the Passport Office always needs a name change certificate from an Australian registry.
Once Australia recognises your Italian marriage you cannot marry each other again here, though a confirmation of vows or recommitment ceremony is open to you.

faq.q: Can you use an Italian marriage certificate to change your name in Australia?
faq.a: It is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but may not work for a name change. NSW and Victoria require a change of name application, and Australian-born passport applicants always need an Australian name change certificate.

faq.q: Is a symbolic wedding in Italy legally binding?
faq.a: No. Australia only recognises a marriage valid under Italian law, and the comune does not register a symbolic ceremony as one. For a symbolic ceremony in Italy, marry legally in Australia first.

faq.q: Can we have a second wedding ceremony in Australia after marrying in Italy?
faq.a: Not a second marriage. You can hold a confirmation of vows or recommitment ceremony, or a religious ceremony under s 113(5) once you show your existing certificate.

faq.q: Does marrying in Italy give my partner a right to live in Australia?
faq.a: No. Smartraveller says marrying an Australian citizen does not ensure entry or citizenship; immigration law still applies.

faq.q: Can you divorce in Australia if you married in Italy?
faq.a: Yes, if one of you is eligible, for example as an Australian citizen. You must have been separated for 12 months and 1 day, and a non-English certificate is filed with a translator's affidavit.
